title: Quick lows before 3.9.0
description: The last phase of 3.9.0: lows whose fix is small and needs no design decision. Each fix closes its class at a shared seam.
desiredOutcome: The quick, decision-free lows left after P163 and P164 are closed: report link decode, side-nav highlight, bugs-table chip wrap, Sort-select coverage, panel arrow a11y, STACK_BUDGET wording, three drive lows, a symlink spelling in start, a test marker.

findings.issue: Link validation is not at one seam: each FILTER_AXES entry's decode re-implements it by hand - five near-identical bodies `if (!offeredBy(<bar>, 'data-<x>').includes(h.<x>)) return false; <state> = h.<x>; return true;` plus bespoke area and date variants - and each re-spells the chip attribute its own `attrs` already declares (a third copy beside `attrs` and `paint`). The registry therefore holds the rule as an enumeration: a new axis whose decode omits the offeredBy call restores any value, and nothing in the code refuses it; only the browser gate's hr1 catches it, through a regex over the source spelling (finding 3). The task asked for the fix 'at the shared seam rather than per instance'.
findings.resolution: Declare what each axis's control offers once, in the entry (e.g. `offers: () => offeredBy(bar, entry.attrs[0], sel)`; search and the date pair declare their own acceptor), and have the one restore loop (exports.js `FILTER_AXES.forEach((axis) => { if (axis.decode(HASH)) ... })`) hand each decode only the HASH values its acceptor admits, so an unoffered value never reaches a decode by construction and the per-axis decodes shrink back to plain assignments. Keep hr1 as the browser-side proof.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Add a browser-gate case that clicks each side-nav entry at more than one width and reads that the highlight names the clicked section': sn1 excuses any entry the document ends before reaching the line and prints it as a note instead of judging it. Re-run on the new acme render: `note side-nav jumps the document ends before: 1512px #bugs (document ends 161px short)` - clicking Bugs at 1512px lights Ready (the end-of-document rule lights the last section), so the highlight does not name the clicked section and sn1 is green over it. The executor flagged this as a design call; the behaviour predates the diff (same on eed7a78b), but the gate as written does not read what the clause asked.
findings.resolution: Recommended: at the end of the document, let the section the reader jumped to (location.hash's target, when its top is on screen) win over 'light the last section', then delete the `short` carve-out so sn1 judges every entry. If the owner prefers the end rule, record that as a decision/fault and keep the note - but then the clause is narrowed by decision, not by the gate.

findings.issue: hr0 derives the link keys by spelling: `/\bkeys: \[([^\]]*)\]/` and `'([a-z]+)'` over the page source. An axis written `keys:['x']`, with a double-quoted key, or a key holding a digit or capital is silently not exercised, and hr0 only asserts HR_KEYS.length > 0, so a dropped key stays green.
findings.resolution: Cross-check the derivation against the registry's own shape: e.g. count the `decode:` members of FILTER_AXES in the source and require one keys match per entry (the empty `keys: []` of task-status included), or tolerate whitespace/quote variants in the regex and fail when an entry yields no match.

findings.issue: The room after the content is a fixed calc(100vh - var(--sticky-anchor)) on every report, whatever the last targets actually need, so scrolling to the end shows a viewport that is mostly blank: measured on the new renders (Playwright, file://, the gate's LAYOUT_SIZES), spacer / blank at bottom-of-scroll / room actually needed for the furthest nav target to reach the line = 390x844 784/896/282 px (93% of vh), 844x390 330/394/27 (85%), 834x1194 1012/1076/709 (85%), 1024x768 586/650/283 (76%), 1512x945 811/875/508 (86%), 1920x1080 946/1010/643 (88%) for acme; docs/demo-large.html gets the identical spacer and blank tail while its needed room is 0 px at every size (every target already reaches the line at HEAD). A reader pressing End on any report sees roughly a screenful of empty page below a few lines of content, and on demo-large it serves no purpose at all. Print is clean: under emulateMedia print the ::after computes content:none, and the A4 PDF page count equals HEAD's (acme 18/18, demo-large 148/148). sn0 pins the CSS string and sn1 only asserts the marker, so nothing bounds the tail.
findings.resolution: Size the room by what the last targets need, not by a viewport: page-state.js already measures the sticky stack and reads the line back (landingLine); publish one custom property, e.g. max(0, innerHeight - line - (content end - furthest nav target's top)), on load and resize and let the screen-only ::after read it (still keyed to --sticky-anchor through the line, so it tracks it). A CSS-only alternative, min-height on the last section, needs the renderer to wrap that section, since .content is flat (H2#ready then DL.ready). Then add a browser-gate bound beside sn1: at every LAYOUT_SIZES size the blank tail at bottom-of-scroll is at most the needed room plus the content's own bottom padding (64 px at HEAD), so demo-large reads ~64 px and acme reads needed+64, and prove it red against this render.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "a browser check ... that the summary's accessible name carries no arrow glyph, red-first on the current panel and report": none of the browser cases the clause asks for (ax4, ax5, pa1) was ever seen red. Attempt 1's redFirst is could-not-prove (the helper refused a CSS file as an inline suite), and attempt 2's red-first covers only the sd5 pin. On the report side the unfixed tree already carried `content:"\25BE" / ""` in report-css/controls.css, so ax4 passes on HEAD as it stands; its red can only come from a mutation, and none was recorded. pa1's red is the HEAD panel (usage-tab.css had `content:"\25BE"` with no alternative), and no run against it was recorded either. As handed, ax4/pa1 are checks only ever seen green.
findings.resolution: Record a red for each in its own driven runtime, restoring in the same command: (a) panel — run `node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs --check` with shared/disclosure.css's `/ ""` alternatives removed (equivalent to HEAD's panel) and show `pa1 ... FAIL` plus a non-zero exit; (b) report — re-render acme with the same mutation and show `ax4` FAIL from check-report-interactive.mjs; (c) ax5 — drop the shared ::after rule and show ax5 FAIL. Assert that the anchor matched once before each mutation, check the file is cmp-equal afterwards, and put command, exit code and failing case id in redFirst.basis.

findings.issue: The new `disclosure.css` row says "The one stylesheet part here" — a present-tense count claim about the directory's contents that goes false the moment a second shared .css part joins, and nothing re-derives it. Comment/doc-only.
findings.resolution: Delete the count: e.g. "A stylesheet part: it joins `_ui_theme.REPORT_CSS_PARTS` and `_ui_theme.PANEL_CSS_PARTS` rather than the two script tuples, ...".

tasks.title: A report link restores only filters a control shows, and the side-nav highlights the section a jump lands on
tasks.description:
Two report behaviour lows, one class each, fixed at the shared seam rather than per instance.

1. A report link can restore a filter no control shows. Hash decode (the FILTER_AXES registry in plugins/audit/scripts/ui/report/page-state.js) accepts values no control offers and hides rows behind them with nothing pressed: `#!m=bogus`, `#!a=nosuch` (unknown model/area), `#!tev=constructor` (a prototype key), `#!from=notadate`, `#!au=nobody` (hides Usage rows). Separately `#!ps=done` is dropped without a word in the Active view. Fix: every axis's decode keeps only values its control offers (read off the control/DOM, own-property lookups only), and what it drops is not applied; the restored state is exactly what the controls show. Decide the ps-in-Active-view case so the user is not silently given a different filter than the link named (e.g. switch the View to one that shows it, or keep it as an honest no-op the counter states) - pick the least surprising, say why in the code comment. Add browser-gate cases in tools/check-report-interactive.mjs: per axis, a bogus value in the hash restores nothing hidden and nothing pressed; red-first them: the render committed at eed7a78b (git show eed7a78b:examples/acme-store/acme-store-audit.html) must fail the new cases; quote the failing lines.

2. The side-nav highlights the section above after a nav jump, at every width: a section's scroll-margin is --sp-2 while markSpy (page-state.js) treats a section as current only past the layers' height + 4px, so a jump lands just short of that line. Fix: derive both from ONE value (one source the CSS scroll-margin and markSpy both read), not two constants kept equal by hand. Add a browser-gate case that clicks each side-nav entry at more than one width and reads that the highlight names the clicked section; red-first it on the current committed render.

Refresh rendered followers (examples/report.sh, docs/demo-large.html via `python3 tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py --how`, `node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs`) so tests/test__refs.py and check-rendered-artifacts stay green. Read writing-javascript, refactoring-the-assembled-ui, no-silent-pass. No register ids in comments.

tasks.title: The drive's base-measure bound reads the red before asking, its documents say the bound, and a wait names a hand-out rather than a launch
tasks.description:
Three drive lows in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py and the documents that describe it.

1. In base_reading_for, the due-branch bound check (around the `unmeasurable_bound` call in the due branch) runs before the red's own reading is read. A `not-knowable` reading already names a base run (base_behind), and the decided-mark branch sends such a red to the writer; so once a start holds UNMEASURED_BOUND moved-code bases, a later not-knowable red gets a spurious `gate-red-base-unknown` ask whose sentence claims the base "could not be measured either". Fix: in the due branch check `unmeasurable_bound(before) and not base_behind(reading)` (read the reading first). Add a twin of the bi16 case in tests/test_drive_phase.py that goes red without the fix (prove it).

2. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (around the base-measure section, near "goes to the writer every time, bounded by the writer rounds") and the block comment above BASE_MEASURE_VERDICTS say an unrunnable red always goes to the writer. That stops being true once a start reaches UNMEASURED_BOUND moved-code bases (the due branch then stops every red of the start before it is measured). Add "until the start reaches the bound" (or equivalent) in both places, matching plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md which already says it correctly.

3. The `wait-gate` and the matching wait line for a phase gate say "the gate launched %(since)s has recorded no run for it yet", but the drive stamps that time when it HANDS OUT the run-test-gate step, not when a gate process starts - so the line asserts a launch it never observed. Fix the claim: word it as what the drive knows ("handed out at %(since)s; no run recorded since") everywhere this stamp is rendered, and keep the remedy rule. Update any test pins on the old wording.

Read writing-python, before-you-claim, no-silent-pass. No register ids in comments.

outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: (1) base_reading_for's due branch now reads the red's own reading before the bound stops it: past unmeasurable_bound, a reading that names a base run (base_behind) returns (None, reading, None) - decided by that reading, with nothing measured - and only a red with no base run gets bound_said's 'could not be measured either' stop. DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF'S LITERAL FIX: the brief said `if unmeasurable_bound(before) and not base_behind(reading)`, which falls through and launches a measurement (inline or background) for that red past the bound, breaking the bound's own contract ('no base run is launched for a red after it' in execute-task.md, 'BEFORE any measurement is launched' in the block comment). The mutation probe proves the literal form launches (bi17 red under it). Behaviour difference is narrow: the red goes to the writer on its own base-run reading, exactly as the decided-mark branch already sends it. (2) Block comment above BASE_MEASURE_VERDICTS and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: 'goes to the writer every time' now carries 'until the start reaches the bound', and both say a red whose reading names a base run is decided by it past the bound; the guide's 'goes to the writer as before' for a moved-code red got the same qualifier (same claim, same class). base_reading_for's docstring says the same. execute-task.md already said it correctly ('no base run is launched for a red after it') and is unchanged. (3) wait-gate line now reads 'the gate was handed out at %(since)s; no run recorded for it since'; wait-base carried the same hand-out stamp (launch_base stamps `at` when it prints the dispatch) so it reads 'the base measurement was handed out at %(since)s; no reading left since'. gate_wait_said/base_wait_said docstrings say the stamp is the hand-out moment, never a process start. Both the task gate and the phase gate render through gate_wait_said, so one template covers both; rules (remedy lines) unchanged. No test pinned the old wording (grep for 'recorded no run', 'left no reading yet', 'measurement launched' over the tree: only the template itself). The guide's wait-gate sentence now says it prints the hand-out moment. Tests: bi17 (in _bi_bound_due_case, the bi16 twin: not-knowable reading with run 'r-base' past the bound -> (None, reading, None), nothing taken or launched, inline and background) and bg2h (in _background_gate_cases after bg2: the real wait block a `next` printed names the launch mark's `at` as 'handed out at <stamp>;' exactly once and has no 'launched'; base_wait_said likewise). tasks.title: start compares the plan directory and the project directory on one path resolution; a test marker is restored
tasks.description:
Two small manifest/test lows.

1. `audit-task.py start` counts the plan's own evidence as undeclared readers when the project directory is spelled through a symlink: the plan-directory exclude is computed from os.path.abspath(mpath), which resolves through the cwd's real path (/private/tmp/...), then taken relative to a --project-dir spelled /tmp/..., so the exclude comes out empty and ~20 files under docs/audit/evidence count as readers and start refuses. Fix: compare both sides on one resolution (os.path.realpath on both, or the module's existing canonical-path helper if one exists - search before adding). Look for the same abspath-vs-realpath mix elsewhere in the start/scope reader path and fix the class with one helper, not per call site. Add a case in tests/test_audit_task.py that builds a project under a symlinked directory and runs start through the symlinked spelling; prove it red without the fix (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp is one such link; build your own symlink under tempfile.mkdtemp() so it is portable, and skip with a printed reason on a platform without symlinks).

2. tests/test_usage_ledger.py has a section marker `# --- rx:the re-export` with the space after the colon dropped by an earlier edit; restore `# --- rx: the re-export`.

Read writing-python and no-silent-pass. No register ids in comments.

Used at both subtractions in the start/scope reader path: _owed_now's plan-directory exclude (the bug: abspath(mpath) resolved through the physical cwd vs a --project-dir spelled through a link climbed out of the project, so the exclude came out empty) and _unanswered_readers' remedy spelling (behaviour-neutral today: git_root is derived from project's own spelling; applied so the reader path has one subtraction). tasks.description:
Three report layout lows, closed together because they share the layout matrix in tools/check-report-interactive.mjs.

1. The bugs table's STATUS chip wraps inside the word at 1440x900 ("Fixe / d", "Won' / t fix") and the ID column breaks "BUG- / 10". Fix in report-css/tables.css: chips and ids do not break inside a word (white-space: nowrap on the chip and id cells, or a min width from the longest chip - whichever keeps the table inside the page at the phone size). Widen the matrix's "no word split across lines" assertion (lm5) from the chrome to EVERY table's chips and ids (phases, tasks, bugs, ready-now, usage), so a table added later is covered by default; red-first it on the current committed acme render and quote the failing lines.

2. The Sort select in the phases table's head renders only when any phase is pinned (any_phase_pinned), and no committed fixture has a pinned phase, so the layout matrix never sees it. Add a pinned phase to the demo-large fixture's generator (tools/demo/gen-demo-manifest.py; re-render docs/demo-large.html via `python3 tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py --how`), and make the matrix FAIL by name on demo-large when no Sort select is present (a fixture that stops carrying it must not pass silently). Keep tests/test_gen_demo_manifest.py green and update its pins honestly.

3. Two wording fixes beside STACK_BUDGET (change no share): (a) the sentence saying a phone whose filter bar wraps one more row fails lm4 - the cheapest row measured is 27.4px against 27px of headroom and lm4's stack is a whole-pixel scan that can sit up to 1.5px off, so only the 32px arm (a row holding the count) is shown to fail; say exactly that; (b) the rule's "over the class's screen height" must read "over that size's height" - a class holds sizes with different heights and lm4 applies the share per size.

tasks.title: Link validation is the registry's, derived from each axis's attrs; every side-nav jump marks its section at every size; hr0 reads the page's own keys
tasks.description:
Fix the P165.1 review's findings on the unlanded diff (ad08e5bc), at the seam, not per axis.

1. Link validation lives at the REGISTRY level in plugins/audit/scripts/ui/report/page-state.js. Today each FILTER_AXES entry's decode re-implements `if (!offeredBy(<bar>, 'data-<x>').includes(h.<x>)) return false` by hand and re-spells the chip attribute its own `attrs` already declares. Make the registry itself keep only values a control offers, derived from each axis's `attrs` (one helper the restore path calls for every axis), so an axis supplies only its genuine exceptions (area's select-backed vocabulary, the date fields' parse) as a declared hook. A new axis written with no hook is validated by default. Add a browser-gate case in tools/check-report-interactive.mjs that goes red when an axis restores an unoffered value: drive EVERY axis in the page's registry with a bogus value and assert nothing is hidden and nothing pressed. Prove it red-first by a mutation: drop the registry-level check on a scratch copy of the new render (or bypass it for one axis) and quote the failing line.

2. Remove the sn1 exemption ("side-nav jumps the document ends before" printed as a note). Give the document enough end space (e.g. padding or a spacer after the last section, sized from the same one value the scroll line uses, so it tracks it) that every section can scroll to the line, so clicking Bugs at 1512x945 marks Bugs, not Ready. Assert, at EVERY size in the layout matrix, that each side-nav click marks the clicked entry - no carve-out. Red-first: the render committed at ad08e5bc must fail at 1512 on Bugs; quote it.

3. hr0 derives link keys with a regex over the page source. Read the keys from the page's own registry at runtime instead (expose a read-only list of axis keys on the page, the same way the gate already reads other runtime state, or evaluate the registry in page context), and fail by name if the page exposes none.

outcome.technical: page-state.js: link validation moved to the registry. offeredBy(axis) derives the vocabulary from the toggles ([aria-pressed][attr]) carrying each axis's declared attrs plus an optional declared `twin` select; keptFromLink(axis, h) keeps per key what the axis's `takes` hook keeps, or with no hook the whole value when offered (takesOffered); FILTER_AXES is built as `[...].map((axis) => ({ ...axis, decode: (h) => axis.decode(keptFromLink(axis, h)) }))`, so every decode, including one added later with no hook, only sees checked values and no caller can bypass it. Entries' decodes went back to plain assignments; the exceptions are declared hooks: search takes free text, area takes tag-by-tag (twin areaSelect), dates take what a date field holds (dateFieldTakes); author declares twin auSelect. The registry publishes its keys as data-link-keys on the root. exports.js (not declared) is untouched; its restore loop still calls axis.decode(HASH), now the wrapped decode. markSpy's end-of-document clamp is removed. shell.css: :root{--sticky-anchor:calc(var(--sticky-2) + var(--sp-2))}, [id]{scroll-margin-top:var(--sticky-anchor)}, and @media screen{.snav ~ .content::after{...height:calc(100vh - var(--sticky-anchor))}}, so every target can reach the one line (named --sticky-* because the theme-symmetry lint treats that prefix as geometry; --anchor-line was flagged as a light-only colour token). Gate: hr0 reads data-link-keys at runtime, fails by name when it is absent, and fails if the free-text exemption ['q'] names a key the page no longer publishes; hr1 is red on an empty key set rather than passing vacuously; sn1 clicks every visible entry at every LAYOUT_SIZES size with the 'document ends before' note/carve-out removed; is11 hovers .snav a at 1000x800 (the strip presentation). Tests: _registry_text tolerates the .map close; new rx10 (check sits once on the registry, no decode reads controls, only area/dates/search declare takes) and sn0 (no end-of-document rule in markSpy, spacer and scroll-margin share --sticky-anchor, screen only); the anchor pin updated to the token. READMEs (report/, report-css/) updated. Followers: examples/report.sh (acme html+md, docs/index.html byte copy), docs/demo-large.html per check-rendered-artifacts --how, node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs (exit 0, 26 png/json rewritten).
